correctness.rationale: Character orthogonality identifies each local covariance with a nonnegative integer Hom-space dimension. An invariant quadratic tensor injects Sym^(j-2)V into Sym^j V; compact-group semisimplicity and the positive dimension difference for dim V >= 2 yield a same-parity direct-summand ladder and the local lower bound. Primewise independence then gives tau(gcd(u,v)) on a common square class, and the exact divisor-sum reindexing gives x log x + O(x). The one-dimensional case is treated separately, and Jensen is used only for q >= 1/2.

originality.rationale: Leung's arXiv:2609.20460v1 identifies orthogonal type as the case E h_2 = 1 and computes the symmetric-square Sato-Tate model exactly, but does not state a universal orthogonal covariance floor or all-orthogonal second-moment lower bound. Searches for Frobenius-Schur, square-class covariance, orthogonal compact-group random multiplicative functions, and even symmetric-power Sato-Tate formulations did not identify prior coverage. The representation-theoretic ingredients themselves are classical. The main residual risk is unindexed contemporaneous work because the source preprint is very recent.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a single orthogonal example to a structural theorem for every nontrivial irreducible orthogonal compact-group model. It proves that prime-square centering is structurally necessary for the centered low-moment scale throughout this Frobenius-Schur class, gives an explicit square-class correlation mechanism, and covers all even symmetric-power Sato-Tate models at once.
